title: Stalkwise Tor dimensions are locally uniformly bounded
statement: Let $X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $Y$ Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], and $f:X\to Y$ locally of finite type. Suppose that every source local ring has finite Tor dimension over its target local ring [def-pc-perfect-morphism]. For every $x\in X$ there are an open $U\subseteq X$ with $x\in U$ and an integer $d\geq0$ such that for every $y\in U$, every $\mathcal O_{Y,f(y)}$-module $M$, and every integer $j>d$, $\operatorname{Tor}^{\mathcal O_{Y,f(y)}}_j(\mathcal O_{X,y},M)=0$. The module structure uses the stalk homomorphism of $f$; the same $d$ works for all $y\in U$ and all $M$. No quasi-compactness of $X$ is assumed.

proof.text: Around the point choose affine source and target neighbourhoods with source algebra B of finite type over the Noetherian target algebra A. Present B as a quotient of a finite polynomial algebra over A. Noetherianity makes B pseudo-coherent over this polynomial algebra. Use the stalkwise finite Tor hypothesis at primes of B. At polynomial primes not meeting the support the localized B-module is zero; at all others its Tor dimension over the corresponding A-localization is finite. Polynomial fibres have finite global dimension, so the localized B-modules are perfect over the localized polynomial algebras. The local criterion for pseudo-coherent modules yields a perfect polynomial module, hence a perfect ring map A to B. This is Tag 069C, implication (3) to (1).

source.place: Tag 069C, lemma-check-perfect-stalks, implication (3) to (2) and (1) to (2); Cohomology Tag 09U9; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/069C

proof.text: A perfect ring map gives a finite Tor bound d for B over A. Localizing at source and image primes preserves this bound. Thus every stalk in the chosen affine source neighbourhood has the same Tor vanishing above d for all target-stalk modules. This is Tag 069C, implication (1) to (2), or its stalk formulation via Tag 09U9. There is no point to check on an empty scheme; no finite cover of the entire source is used.

from.place: Relative finite Tor part of the proper perfect pushforward argument descending from lem-sc-finite-duality; step 1 of lem-pc-perfect-relative-tensor-locally-bounded (Tag 069C, stalkwise finite Tor dimension to a uniform neighbourhood bound).

lean.statement:
theorem stalkTorDimension_locally_uniform
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian Y]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (hperfect : HasStalkwiseFiniteTorDimension f) :
    ∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ ∃ d : ℕ,
      ∀ y : X, y ∈ U → ∀ M : ModuleCat.{u} (Y.presheaf.stalk (f y)),
        ∀ j : ℕ, d < j →
          IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} (Y.presheaf.stalk (f y))) j).obj
            ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (f.stalkMap y).hom).obj
              (ModuleCat.of (X.presheaf.stalk y) (X.presheaf.stalk y)))).obj M)
